_note: THE ODIN DEPLOYMENT CELL — the recipe for the FIRST bundle cut from a real trained network, and it is CONV-FIRST. MEASURED 2026-08-28, end to end, exit 0. WHY NOT THE OLD OCCUPANT: this file used to hold the withdrawn MLP tier row t0_55, blocked twice at the stock core (wb=4 per_axon took it 0.9314 -> 0.6117 at Weight Quantization, then NF<->SCM parity refused at 0.7969 against 0.9). WHY NOT LENET5: the stock crossbar is 256 PHYSICAL rows and the per-axon sign expansion spends two per logical slot, so a core holds 128 logical axons and 127 effective without a bias lane; lenet5's flatten->FC junction is ONE 785-axon soft core (1570 physical rows, 6.1x the crossbar) and, with no inter-core membrane partial-sum transfer to coalesce into, the mapper refuses it outright — measured, on the committed shapes, before any training. Its two MaxPool stages also split the program into TWO neural segments and a bundle freezes one. WHAT THE PER-EVENT LAW ADDS: export_odin deploys only firing_granularity=per_event, and the event-serial training twin folds a hop only when its effective weight spans its WHOLE input and its upstream is another hop — so a 3x3 conv over a 7x7 map is refused by the TWIN (not by ODIN: that core fits at 127 axons), and so is a Flatten between two hops. narrow_conv states both: a conv stem the subsume placement hands to the host, a collapse conv over the whole residual extent, pointwise trunk stages, a pointwise ACTIVATED readout so the class scores stay on a spiking core for the bundle's argmax rule. GEOMETRY (measured before training): 2 cores in ONE neural segment — core 0 at 127 logical axons / 254 physical rows / 120 neurons, core 1 at 121 / 242 / 10.
